answer: A piecewise-defined function is a function that is defined by different formulas on different parts of its domain. An example of this is the absolute value function, which changes its formula based on the sign of the input. Additionally, other piecewise-defined functions may use completely different formulas depending on the specific part of the domain in which a point falls [openstax_calculus_v1_p0051_s0_paragraph_0001].
